title: Regina Home Rebates 2026: SaskEnergy Furnace and Boiler Rebates
desc: Regina home rebates for 2026: older homes mean more furnace and boiler replacements, and SaskEnergy pays $325 to $1,000 for high-efficiency gas equipment. Rules, efficiency levels and who can apply.
lead: More than half of Regina's homes were built before 1981, and 7% needed major repairs, the highest share of any Saskatchewan city we looked at. That means many Regina furnaces and boilers are due for replacement, which is exactly what SaskEnergy's rebate pays for. Here is how it works on October 21, 2026.
cards_heading: What is open for Regina homes in 2026
cards_intro: We read the SaskPower and SaskEnergy pages on October 21, 2026. Each card shows the date and links to the source.

cards.title: Gas furnace
cards.note: 97% AFUE or higher, on SaskEnergy's list. Licensed gas contractor.

cards.title: Boiler or water heater
cards.note: Boiler $750, combi boiler $800, tankless or condensing water heater $1,000.

cards.title: Free upgrades
cards.note: SaskPower Energy Assistance Program. Homeowners, renters and landlords.

cards.title: Retrofit rebate
cards.note: SaskPower's Home Efficiency Retrofit Rebate has ended.

cards.title: Heat pump, insulation, windows
cards.note: We found no SaskPower or SaskEnergy rebate for these on October 21, 2026.

sections:
The 2021 Census counted 92,130 households in the City of Regina.

  • Older homes. 50,135 homes (54%) were built before 1981.
  • Houses. 58,120 households (63%) live in single-detached houses, a higher share than in Saskatoon.
  • Owners. 66% own and 34% rent.
  • Repairs. 6,725 homes (7%) needed major repairs.

The median household total income was $88,000 in 2020, before tax, and about 24% of households earned under $50,000.

SaskEnergy's Residential Equipment Replacement Rebate pays for replacing natural gas equipment that is part of your primary space or water heating system:

EquipmentMinimum efficiencyRebate
Furnace97.0% AFUE$325
Boiler, per plant up to 300 MBH95.0% AFUE$750
Combi boiler95.0% AFUE$800
Tankless water heater0.87 UEF$1,000
Condensing water heater0.80 UEF$1,000

The revised terms took effect August 17, 2026, and the efficiency bar for furnaces is now 97.0%. A 96% furnace that earned a rebate before may not qualify now. SaskEnergy pays the amount in effect on the day it receives your complete application.

SaskEnergy describes the rebate as a payment to partially offset the higher purchase price of higher efficiency units. It is not meant to cover the whole bill, and it does not cover the contractor's labour on its own. With so many older Regina homes, the practical order is to ask your contractor three things before you sign: whether the exact model is on SaskEnergy's eligible equipment list, whether your existing unit is out of manufacturer's warranty, and who will file the application. The program says a contractor may apply on your behalf, and the eligibility of a unit and the amount are set by the rules and rebate schedule in effect on the day SaskEnergy receives the application, so file promptly after installation.
Who can apply, and the rules that catch people out

You must be the person who pays the invoice and be a registered homeowner, landlord or rental company, and a SaskEnergy residential customer. A contractor may apply for you. The home must be in Saskatchewan, and new construction is not eligible. Row housing and duplex units count if each has its own meter. Garages, including attached ones, do not. The equipment you replace must be out of manufacturer's warranty. Used or rebuilt units, self-installs, gifts and contest prizes are not eligible, but units bought at auction and units covered by an insurance claim are, with the invoice. You have 120 days from installation, and approved rebates arrive within 6 weeks.
Free help, and what has ended

SaskPower's Energy Assistance Program is free and open to homeowners, renters and landlords. SaskPower's Home Efficiency Retrofit Rebate ended in April 2026. We found no provincial heat pump, insulation or window rebate. That is a negative result, not proof that none exists. Ottawa's National Heat Pump Rebate is expected in early 2027. See our National Heat Pump Rebate guide.
claim_steps: Check the age and warranty status of your furnace, boiler or water heater.
Look up the new unit on SaskEnergy's eligible equipment list.
Hire a gas contractor with a TSASK licence.
Apply within 120 days with the invoice.
Ask about the free Energy Assistance Program as well.
faq: What furnace efficiency does SaskEnergy require now?
97.0% AFUE or better since the terms changed on August 17, 2026. The rebate is $325.
Can a Regina landlord get the SaskEnergy rebate?
Yes. Landlords and rental companies that pay the invoice and are SaskEnergy residential customers can apply.
Does a duplex qualify in Regina?
Row housing and duplex units qualify if each unit has its own dedicated meter.
How long does the rebate take?
SaskEnergy says it pays within 6 weeks of receiving and approving the application, which must arrive within 120 days of installation.
Is there a Regina city home energy rebate?
We found no City of Regina home energy rebate on SaskPower's or SaskEnergy's pages.
